title.narrative: Strengthening Capacity of Maritime Law Enforcement Agencies for Effective Maritime Crime Control in the South East Asia and Pacific Island Countries

description.narrative:
The Global Maritime Crime Programme (GMCP) of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
(UNODC) initiated the project “Capacity Strengthening for Maritime Law Enforcement Agencies of the
Pacific Island Countries to Efficiently Counter Maritime Crime'' in 2023. This project is aimed at providing
multifaceted support to maritime law enforcement forces of the Pacific. In particular, the project aims to
equip maritime law enforcement forces with necessary MDA analytical skills, better understanding of
criminality methods, and firsthand experiences for better tactics and operation in countering drug
trafficking at sea. Regarding fisheries enforcement, the UNODC GMCP will focus on enhancing Maritime
Surveillance capabilities through different types of training and equipment support for the DFIRES and
related maritime surveillance agencies.
While law enforcement officers are at the frontline of national and regional security, supporting their
operational capacities would not yield in meaningful and structural changes if the overall justice systems
are not equipped to effectively deliver justice on maritime crime cases. International cooperation between
justice institutions in this regard would also be important as maritime criminal cases are often
transboundary in nature. The project also incorporates technical assistance to criminal justice practitioners
dealing with maritime crime cases.

Under its ongoing project, GMCP must procure USD 1,970,000 worth of equipment and services to be able to implement its planned activities.
